job.rawJd: Bnberry is transforming the $87 billion travel tech industry by changing how hotels and resorts connect with guests worldwide. The role owns DBS end to end across the traveler booking experience, hotel workflows and business value, and hotel discovery through search and AI tools. Responsibilities include defining product vision and roadmap; owning calendars, date selection, room and rate selection, checkout, confirmation, availability, rates, cancellation policies, and PMS/CRS or booking-engine dependencies; translating hotel onboarding, reporting, and adoption needs into product decisions; partnering with Marketing and specialists on SEO and GEO capabilities; interviewing hoteliers and travelers; running usability tests; defining success metrics before building; using experiment results to guide iteration; working with Design and Engineering through detailed user journeys; aligning Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success; and taking responsibility for product outcomes. Requirements include three or more years of product management experience owning customer-facing products, with relevant hospitality technology or travel-booking experience; a demonstrable US-market connection; hands-on research; analytical and experimentation skills; comfort with detailed user journeys and practical iteration; and the ability to work independently through ambiguity. The ideal candidate has worked in hotel technology, B2B hospitality platforms, or a B2C travel product with an actual booking journey. Deep hotel-distribution-system exposure is a plus rather than a prerequisite. The candidate should be fluent in both traveler and hotel needs and able to learn emerging SEO and GEO capabilities without personally executing SEO.

paragraphs: I am applying for Bnberry's Product Manager role with a clear understanding of the domain gap in my background: I have not worked on lodging platforms or owned a live reservation funnel. What I do bring is the product work around that domain: customer research, detailed journey and workflow design, product prioritization, adoption, analytics, and cross-functional delivery from discovery through working software.

At Kinesso, I built the first UX research practice across more than 20 products and led research and experience strategy for an enterprise platform suite used by more than 7,000 people across 22 brands. Interviews, prototype testing, beta groups, behavioral analytics, and adoption data shaped roadmap priorities for navigation, dashboards, personalization, and product support. I also helped turn channel scoring, benchmarks, and recommendations into a repeatable client-facing reporting workflow. That work taught me how to connect user friction, platform constraints, adoption, and business value in one product decision.

Today, through One Block Away, I own product strategy, UX, AI workflow design, front-end build, backend logic, demos, and client iteration from first ask through working prototype. ListingPal turns basic property inputs into MLS and SEO-ready content in under 90 seconds. Other products have started with an unclear business problem and become a structured workflow, testable product surface, and practical roadmap. That gives me a useful base for working with Marketing and specialists on search and AI discovery without claiming to be an SEO practitioner.

The lodging-specific learning curve would be the systems and commercial rules behind inventory, pricing, policy exceptions, failure cases, and funnel metrics. My way into a new domain is direct: interview the people who run it, map the exceptions, work through dependencies with Engineering, establish a baseline, ship a small change, and measure what happened. I have used that method across regulated healthcare and enterprise platforms. I would welcome a conversation about applying it to the guest journey and hotel workflows behind DBS.

resume.summary: Product and experience strategy lead with 15 years across customer research, enterprise platforms, AI implementation, and client delivery. I connect customer research, workflow design, adoption data, and practical AI implementation to turn unclear needs into testable products and roadmap decisions. Recent work includes user interviews, usability testing, behavioral analytics, working POCs, and enterprise products used by 7,000+ people across 22 brands.
